title: Plans and wishes
summary: Say what you want to do, suggest doing it together, and say how often you do things.
canDo: I can say what I want and do not want to do.
I can suggest a plan, fix a time and say I am going somewhere to do something.
I can say how often I do things: often, sometimes, not much, never.
grammar: よく・ときどき・あまり・ぜんぜん

items.back: I want to ~. Take the ます form, drop ます and add たいです: {行|い}きます → {行|い}きたいです.
I don't want to ~. たい changes like an い-adjective.

items.front: {写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ります

items.back: Let's ~. Replace ます with ましょう.
Shall we ~? Used to settle the details of a plan.
To go and do something: verb without ます, then に{行|い}きます. {見|み}に{行|い}きます = go to see.

items.front: よく・ときどき・あまり・ぜんぜん
items.back: How often. よく (often) and ときどき (sometimes) go with a positive verb; あまり (not much) and ぜんぜん (never) need a negative.
not at all, never (with a negative)

lessons.title: I want to see Mount Fuji
lessons.canDo: I can say what I want and do not want to do.

intro.scene: Friday evening. Sato asks Leo what he would like to do with his free weekend.

lines.text: レオさん、{週末|しゅうまつ}{は|wa}{何|なに}がしたいですか。
lines.meaning: Leo, what do you want to do at the weekend?

lines.text: {富士山|ふじさん}が{見|み}たいです。
lines.meaning: I want to see Mount Fuji.

lines.text: いいですね。{登|のぼ}りたいですか。
lines.meaning: Nice. Do you want to climb it?

lines.text: いいえ、{登|のぼ}りたくないです。{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}りたいです。
lines.meaning: No, I don't want to climb it. I want to take photos.

lines.text: {何|なに}が{食|た}べたいですか。
lines.meaning: What do you want to eat?

lines.text: おいしい{寿司|すし}が{食|た}べたいです！
lines.meaning: I want to eat good sushi!

notes.title: Making 〜たい
notes.body: Take any ます verb, remove ます and add たいです: {行|い}きます → {行|い}きたいです, {食|た}べます → {食|た}べたいです, します → したいです.

notes.title: It behaves like an い-adjective
notes.body: So the negative is 〜たくないです ({登|のぼ}りたくないです) and the past is 〜たかったです ({行|い}きたかったです, "I wanted to go").

notes.title: が or を, and whose wish
notes.body: The thing you want can take が or を: {寿司|すし}が{食|た}べたいです. Use たい for your own wishes and for asking friends. To a customer or a superior it is too direct.

exercises.explain: たい works like an い-adjective: たくないです.

lessons.title: Let's go! Making a plan
lessons.canDo: I can suggest a plan, fix a time, and say I am going somewhere to do something.

intro.scene: Nakamura runs into Leo at the station and has an idea for Saturday.

lines.text: レオさん、{土曜日|どようび}に{一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}に{行|い}きませんか。
lines.meaning: Leo, won't you come and see a film with me on Saturday?

lines.text: いいですね。{行|い}きましょう！
{何時|なんじ}に{会|あ}いましょうか。
いいですよ。{映画|えいが}の{後|あと}で、ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べに{行|い}きましょう。
lines.meaning: That's fine. After the film, let's go and eat.

notes.title: 〜ましょう and 〜ましょうか
notes.body: ましょう is "let's": {行|い}きましょう, {食|た}べましょう. With か it asks the other person to decide: {何時|なんじ}に{会|あ}いましょうか, "what time shall we meet?". To invite, 〜ませんか is the softest.

notes.title: Going in order to do something
notes.body: Verb without ます, then に, then {行|い}きます: {見|み}に{行|い}きます (go to see), {食|た}べに{行|い}きます (go to eat), {買|か}いに{行|い}きます (go to buy).

notes.title: Days of the week
notes.body: They all end in {曜日|ようび}: {月曜日|げつようび}, {火曜日|かようび}, {水曜日|すいようび}, {木曜日|もくようび}, {金曜日|きんようび}, {土曜日|どようび}, {日曜日|にちようび}. Like clock times, they take に: {土曜日|どようび}に.

lessons.title: Often, sometimes, never
lessons.canDo: I can say how often I do things.

intro.scene: Leo and Sato compare their free time.

lines.text: レオさん{は|wa}よく{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ますか。
lines.meaning: Do you often watch films, Leo?

lines.text: はい、よく{見|み}ます。{佐藤|さとう}さん{は|wa}？
わたし{は|wa}あまり{見|み}ません。でも、{本|ほん}{は|wa}{毎日|まいにち}{読|よ}みます。
lines.meaning: I don't watch many. But I read books every day.

lines.text: すごいですね。スポーツ{は|wa}しますか。
lines.meaning: Impressive. Do you do any sport?

lines.text: ときどきテニスをします。レオさん{は|wa}？
lines.meaning: I sometimes play tennis. And you?

lines.text: わたし{は|wa}ぜんぜんしません。でも、サッカー{は|wa}よく{見|み}ます！
lines.meaning: I never do. But I watch football a lot!

notes.title: Four steps
notes.body: {毎日|まいにち} every day · よく often · ときどき sometimes · あまり not much · ぜんぜん never. They go before the verb or before the object: よく{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ます.

notes.title: The last two need a negative
notes.body: あまり{見|み}ません (I don't watch much), ぜんぜんしません (I never do it). With a positive verb they are wrong.

notes.title: {は|wa} for contrast
notes.body: {本|ほん}{は|wa}{毎日|まいにち}{読|よ}みます: "books, on the other hand, I read every day". When you compare two things, を often turns into {は|wa}.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap.
exercises.text: わたし{は|wa}___{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ません。
exercises.explain: Only ぜんぜん fits a negative verb here.

exercises.prompt: "I sometimes play tennis."
options: ときどきテニスをします。
ときどきテニスをしません。
ぜんぜんテニスをします。

exercises.prompt: Build: "I read books every day."
exercises.answer: {毎日|まいにち}{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みます
alt: {本|ほん}を{毎日|まいにち}{読|よ}みます

exercises.prompt: Listen. How often does Sato watch films?
exercises.text: わたし{は|wa}あまり{見|み}ません。

exercises.prompt: Which word must go with a negative verb?
Fill the gap.
exercises.text: レオさん{は|wa}サッカーを___{見|み}ます。

exercises.prompt: Type in Japanese: "I read every day."
Match.

meme.bottom: ぜんぜんしません. But I have opinions about every match.
